title: It survived three Mondays
topic: A vague task that never gets started

pitchScores.hook: "Work on report" has been on your list since September.
Here we observe the human, moving one task to tomorrow.
Rating your excuses for not starting.

hookHeadline: "Work on report" has been on your list since September.
narrationScript: "Work on report" has been on your list since September. It survived three Mondays. It survived a new notebook. It survived you colour-coding the list instead of doing the list. It will outlive us all, unless it gets a first step. "Open the draft. Type one heading." That one's gone by lunch. Try the audit at moltology.org.
scenePrompts: Close-up of a hand dragging a sticky note reading only a scribble from one calendar week to the next, the note already curling with age, warm amber desk lamp, deep teal shadows, the motion already underway in the first frame
The same sticky note on a wall calendar as three Monday squares flip past behind it, the note unmoved and faintly smug, slow push-in
A brand-new notebook is opened with ceremony; the old sticky note is transferred onto its first page, unchanged
Overhead shot of a to-do list being colour-coded with four highlighters while the curled note sits untouched in the middle
The friendly cartoon lobster engineer peels the note off the page, crosses out the scribble and writes two short lines in its place
The lobster opens a laptop, types a single heading into a blank document and leans back as the old note drops into a bin, cool ocean light rising
caption:
"Work on report" has been on your list since September.

It has survived three Mondays and a new notebook. Give it a first step you can actually do: open the draft and type one heading.

Try the audit at moltology.org.
youtubeDescription: A vague task survives forever. A first step doesn't. Try the audit: https://moltology.org/quiz
characterArc: Lobster Engineer rewrites a vague task as one visible first step
